research_data.mission_values: Suncorp's purpose is to build futures and protect what matters – a focus maintained for over 100 years. Following the sale of its insurance arm to Allianz, the Group is refocusing squarely on banking. Core values emphasise customer-centricity, trust, empowerment, flexibility, diversity of thought as the key to innovation, and bringing your whole, authentic self to work. The company champions a workplace culture where every voice is heard, actions matter, and employees can make a difference to thousands of customers each day.
research_data.culture_overview: Suncorp operates with a workplace culture built on trust, empowerment, and flexibility designed to help employees unlock their full potential. The organisation values every perspective and listens to every voice, idea, and opinion, recognising diversity of thought as the key to innovation and transformation. Cross-functional integration is central to work practices – designers work seamlessly with Product Managers, Developers, UX Researchers, and Content Strategists in an Agile environment. Design critique culture encourages constructive dialogue and shared learning, with regular feedback sessions and design reviews. Employees are trusted to work flexibly and design their career pathways in ways that work best for them. The culture emphasises collaboration over silos, with room to thrive and explore opportunities at every career stage.

research_data.strategic_plan: Suncorp is in the midst of a major digital transformation, repositioning as a banking-focused organisation following the divestment of its insurance operations. The Digital Experience team is central to this strategy, tasked with reimagining customer interactions across digital channels (web, mobile app, and emerging platforms) to modernise the banking experience for millions of Australians. Investment in design systems ('Spark'), cross-functional Agile squads, and accessibility standards signals a long-term commitment to design maturity. The strategic direction emphasises innovation, customer-centricity, and leveraging technology to differentiate in the competitive Australian banking landscape. Career development pathways, diversity and inclusion initiatives, and flexible working models are integral to attracting and retaining talent to support this transformation agenda.
research_data.interview_focus: Suncorp's interview process for UX/UI designers centres on portfolio review demonstrating end-to-end design thinking – from research through to high-fidelity UI and developer handoff. Expect multi-stage evaluation including initial HR screening (background, tool proficiency, experience), hiring manager discussion (design background, career goals), and portfolio presentation to a panel of designers and product team members. Key assessment areas include: (1) Design process – ability to show research → ideation → testing → iteration, not just final screens; (2) User research capability – planning and conducting research independently, translating findings into design decisions; (3) Collaboration skills – working effectively within Agile squads with product managers, engineers, and content designers; (4) Accessibility knowledge – applying WCAG 2.1 AA standards in shipped products; (5) Communication – articulating design rationale clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leadership (GM level); (6) Tool mastery – advanced Figma proficiency including component libraries, auto layout, variables, Dev Mode; (7) Design systems thinking – contributing to and extending large-scale enterprise systems. Cultural fit assessment focuses on customer-centricity, constructive collaboration, ability to receive feedback, and alignment with Suncorp's values of trust, empowerment, and diversity of thought. Prior financial services experience is regarded highly but not essential if strong design methodology and problem-solving skills are demonstrated. Expect questions on handling complexity, balancing business requirements with user needs, and working within regulatory constraints.
research_data.hiring_unit_intelligence: The Digital Experience — Banking & Wealth team is the specialised business unit responsible for designing customer interactions with Suncorp Bank across all digital channels following the Group's strategic pivot from insurance to banking-focused operations. This unit operates cross-functional Agile squads embedding designers alongside product managers, engineers, data analysts, and content designers. The team owns the 'Spark' design system (Figma-based) and is charged with reimagining the digital banking experience for 1.8 million customers. The Design Lead, Digital Banking (the reporting manager for this role) oversees design delivery and is likely part of a broader design leadership structure that includes design operations, research specialists, and content design functions. The unit emphasises evidence-based design (research + analytics via Amplitude/Google Analytics), accessibility compliance (WCAG 2.1 AA), and developer collaboration via Figma Dev Mode. Design critiques, knowledge-sharing sessions, and mentorship of junior designers are part of the team culture. The unit is distributed across Brisbane and Melbourne hubs with hybrid working (3 days in office). Recent outputs have earned recognition at Good Design Awards 2025 and industry awards, indicating design maturity and investment in craft. The team operates within the regulated environment of Australian banking (APRA prudential standards), requiring designers who can balance innovation with compliance and security requirements.

sources.title: What is going on with the Australian UX & product design job market? Some hypothesises.
sources.snippet: Banks have started to shift technology roles to India and Vietnam. Execution-heavy roles such as UI design and development have been most affected, while strategic and regulated work tended to remain onshore. The shift from 'UX Designer' to 'Product Designer' reframed expectations. Many organisations began to equate the role with UI design and delivery, sidelining research and strategy.
